questions.question:
1.1
The energy diagram below (NOT drawn to scale) shows the electron energies in different energy levels, E1, E2 and E3, of a certain atom.

E3 = 5.7 × 10⁻¹⁹ J
E2 = 5.1 × 10⁻¹⁹ J
E1 = 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ J

An electron of this atom moves from E3 to E1. Photon X is emitted.

Calculate the frequency of photon X.

(4)
questions.answer:
1.1

OPTION 1
E = hf
5.7 × 10⁻¹⁹ − 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴)f
f = 6.64 × 10¹⁴ Hz

OPTION 2
ΔE = E1 − E3
= 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ − 5.7 × 10⁻¹⁹
= −4.4 × 10⁻¹⁹ J
E = hf
4.4 × 10⁻¹⁹ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴)f
f = 6.64 × 10¹⁴ Hz
f must be positive

(4)

questions.question:

(2)

The energy diagram below shows the electron energies in different energy levels, E1, E2, E3 and E4, of a certain atom.

E4 = 8.0 × 10⁻¹⁹ J
E3 = 5.5 × 10⁻¹⁹ J
E2 = 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ J
E1 = 0 J (ground state)

1.3.1 Calculate the energy of the photon emitted when an electron moves from E4 to E2.

1.3.2 Calculate the wavelength of the photon emitted in 1.3.1.

1.3.3 Calculate the frequency of the photon emitted when an electron moves from E3 to E1.

(10)

1.4
The energy levels of a hydrogen atom are given by the equation En = −13.6/n² eV, where n is the principal quantum number.

1.4.1 Calculate the energy of the ground state (n = 1) in joules.

1.4.2 Calculate the energy of the first excited state (n = 2) in joules.

1.4.3 Calculate the energy of the photon emitted when an electron transitions from n = 3 to n = 2.

1.4.4 Calculate the wavelength of the photon emitted in 1.4.3.

(10)

1.5
The energy diagram below shows the first four energy levels of a certain atom.

E4 = 12.0 eV
E3 = 9.0 eV
E2 = 5.0 eV
E1 = 0 eV (ground state)

1.5.1 How many possible spectral lines can be emitted when electrons transition from higher to lower energy levels?

1.5.2 Calculate the energy of the photon with the highest frequency.

1.5.3 Calculate the energy of the photon with the longest wavelength.

(8)
questions.answer:
1.5.1

Number of possible transitions = n(n − 1)/2
= 4(4 − 1)/2
= 4(3)/2
= 6 spectral lines

(2)

1.5.2

Highest frequency corresponds to the largest energy transition.
ΔE = E4 − E1
ΔE = 12.0 − 0
ΔE = 12.0 eV
ΔE = (12.0)(1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹)
ΔE = 1.92 × 10⁻¹⁸ J

(3)

1.5.3

Longest wavelength corresponds to the smallest energy transition.
ΔE = E4 − E3
ΔE = 12.0 − 9.0
ΔE = 3.0 eV
ΔE = (3.0)(1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹)
ΔE = 4.8 × 10⁻¹⁹ J

(3)

(8)
